Calculate panel lags, leads and differences

Source: R/panel.R
panel.Rd

Time-aware versions of dplyr::lag() and dplyr::lead(), following Stata's time-series operators after xtset. Values are found by time rather than row position, so gaps give missing values and row order does not matter. Use them in dplyr::mutate() with the panel identifier in .by or dplyr::group_by().

  • stata_lag(): Retrieve the value from n periods earlier.

  • stata_lead(): Retrieve the value from n periods later.

  • stata_diff(): Calculate the nth difference; the default first difference subtracts the previous period's value from the current value.

Usage

stata_lag(x, n = 1L, time, delta = 1, unit = NULL)

stata_lead(x, n = 1L, time, delta = 1, unit = NULL)

stata_diff(x, n = 1L, time, delta = 1, unit = NULL)

Arguments

x

A vector. stata_diff() needs a numeric, logical, Date, date-time or difftime vector.

n

A single non-negative whole number: the number of periods (stata_lag(), stata_lead()) or the difference order (stata_diff()).

time

The time variable, unique within each panel. Supported types:

  • numbers, including labelled numbers and Stata %tm, %tq or %ty variables read by haven, which arrive as plain numbers;

  • Date and date-times (POSIXct/POSIXlt), with unit;

  • period classes, which need no unit: tsibble's yearweek(), yearmonth() and yearquarter(), and zoo's yearmon and yearqtr;

  • ordered factors, such as survey waves, where each level is one period in level order, so an unused level is a gap.

Missing times give missing results, except for zero-order differences. Text and unordered factors are not accepted, because their sorted order need not be the time order ("W10" sorts before "W2"); convert them first, for example with as.numeric(as.character(year)) or factor(wave, levels, ordered = TRUE).

delta

The length of one period in units of time (or of unit), like the delta() option of xtset. For example, delta = 5 for data every five years.

unit

For Date and date-time times, the period: "day" (the default for dates), "week", "month", "quarter" or "year", and for date-times also "second" (their default), "minute" and "hour". Times are compared by whole periods, as with Stata's %tw, %tm, %tq and %ty dates, so any day in March is one month after any day in February. Weeks follow Stata's %tw: each year has 52 weeks starting on 1 January, so the last week has 8 or 9 days (tsibble's yearweek() keeps its ISO weeks). For date-times, seconds measure elapsed time; minute and larger periods use the local clock of their time zone. Must be NULL for numbers and period classes.

Value

A vector with the length and row order of x, with NA where the required period is absent or time is missing. Lags and leads retain the type and attributes of x. Positive-order differences return doubles, or difftime for dates, date-times and difftime input.

With stata_diff(n = 0), numeric/logical inputs return doubles and calendar/duration inputs retain their class (POSIXlt becomes POSIXct). Missing times do not mask values in this case.

Details

  • stata_lag(x, n, time = t) is Ln.x: the value at time t - n * delta.

  • stata_lead(x, n, time = t) is Fn.x: the value at time t + n * delta.

  • stata_diff(x, n, time = t) is Dn.x: the nth difference, so stata_diff(x, time = t) is x - L.x and stata_diff(x, 2, time = t) is D.(D.x).

Compared with dplyr::lag(): lag(x, order_by = year) takes the previous row after sorting, so after a gap (2002, then 2004) it returns the 2002 value as the lag of 2004, and it silently accepts repeated years or a forgotten .by. stata_lag(x, time = year) takes the value at year - 1, returns NA across the gap, and errors on repeated times, as Stata's L.x does. The two agree on sorted, gap-free panels. For irregular event sequences, where the previous record is wanted however long ago it was, use dplyr::lag().

Time values must be unique within each panel (within the whole vector when there is no grouping), as Stata requires with "repeated time values within panel"; check them first with isid(), such as isid(data, id, year). Numeric times are matched exactly, so steps such as 0.1 should be rescaled to whole numbers first.

See also

Other variable generation functions: as_dummy(), cut, row_egen, std()

Examples

panel <- tibble::tibble(
  id = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2),
  year = c(2001, 2002, 2004, 2001, 2002),
  x = c(10, 12, 15, 20, 21)
)
# 2004 has no 2003, so its lag is missing, unlike dplyr::lag()
dplyr::mutate(
  panel,
  lag_x = stata_lag(x, time = year),
  lead_x = stata_lead(x, time = year),
  d_x = stata_diff(x, time = year),
  .by = id
)
#> # A tibble: 5 x 6
#>      id  year     x lag_x lead_x   d_x
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1  2001    10    NA     12    NA
#> 2     1  2002    12    10     NA     2
#> 3     1  2004    15    NA     NA    NA
#> 4     2  2001    20    NA     21    NA
#> 5     2  2002    21    20     NA     1

# Monthly data stored as dates
sales <- tibble::tibble(
  month = as.Date(c("2024-01-31", "2024-02-29", "2024-04-30")),
  amount = c(5, 7, 4)
)
dplyr::mutate(
  sales,
  previous = stata_lag(amount, time = month, unit = "month")
)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 3
#>   month      amount previous
#>   <date>      <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 2024-01-31      5       NA
#> 2 2024-02-29      7        5
#> 3 2024-04-30      4       NA
